notes: Each row is a distinct abstract language-contact unit, not a day, lesson, quest, scene or NPC interaction.

introduce_m lists first R according to LANGUAGE_MAP; introduce_g lists first meaningful R of G according to LANGUAGE_PROGRESSION; first_p lists first independent productive intent for 42 M, never for receptive-only M.
revisit_m is a proposed opportunity to reuse an earlier M with a changed context; not evidence of mastery or a performed test.
The short contrasts are semantic-design tests, not language-parser whitelists; examples may use familiar lexical placeholders.
Load must be judged as a vector of independent dimensions; counts of M/G IDs are planning proxies, NOT calibrated difficulty.
A second independent-P opportunity was added at P2b for location and P3c for preferences, to avoid packing multiple first productive intentions into the same unit.
lexical_anchors are selected expression *candidates* from the 29-group independent language catalogue, NOT a hard number of new words in a day; context_optional is never a requirement.

A few elementary expressions are placed earlier than their catalogue group horizon because the independent M/G map uses them earlier (e.g. ich/du, verstehen, heute/morgen); this is deliberate and must not be confused with teaching entire theme early.
Contemporary lesson/domain examples inside one unit are alternative variants, not simultaneous mandatory unknown vocabulary; background R/E grammar does not create forced productive form.
P6 has distributed integration rather than a single nine-target mega-test: a P6 unit contains at most five planned revisits and never new required M/G.
outcome_candidates provide earlier practice and P6 transfer candidates for each 6 R + 7 W LO; they are not an exam, passing score or proof of mastery.
Independent first-R prerequisites for M08/M22/M27/M30/M55 and G24/G25/G32 are explicitly covered by the lexical anchor schedule.
P1 load smoothed: bringen is first semantically needed with a recipient, krank is introduced in a short personal-message genre; early A0 still has brauchen/Wasser and müde.
53 neutral German contrast pairs from the temporary 53-unit draft were merged into this canonical 73-unit plan; no other language plan is authoritative.
language_example_checks are proposed German A/B substitutions and do not demonstrate empirical understanding or engine/parser support.
Every one of the 73 units now has at least one independent German A/B example; examples are candidate stimuli and not empirically validated difficulty.
A qualitative goal-alignment review replaced mismatched German contrast pairs in 12 units; semantic plausibility is not empirical A0 validation.

Repeated identical German A/B stimuli were separated across neighboring abilities: naming vs command, quality vs state, question target, destination vs location, interest R vs P, and late transfer of M34/M36/M38 and M14/M53.

rules: All cases are language-only contexts with interchangeable names/objects; they neither define NPC biographies nor the game narrative.
For R, German input carries critical facts that are not exposed in Russian instruction/visual highlights.
For W, abstract context facts are the player's observations, not German phrases to copy; receiver lacks these facts.
A/B must differ meaningfully; when multiple slots are relevant, grading evaluates all slots, not merely the changed one.
Parser uncertainty triggers clarification or neutral reformulation, never an automatic 'wrong German' verdict.
The exam remains resittable and separated from the main-path F1 help. Cutoffs and actual exam format remain unapproved.
These are 13 outcome case blueprints, not 13 mandated separate quests or a limit of one test per outcome.

M05 остаётся правом попросить повторение только при реальном непонимании.

a0_early_review.conclusion: No hard blocker from storyline; all nine require F1/interaction validation before asserting true A0 readiness. Neither time nor comprehension were measured.
